detailed_rationale: [DATA] Godrej Properties delivered a record FY26: booking value (pre-sales) of Rs 34,171 Cr (+16% YoY, 105% of guidance, 17,515 units / 27 msf, volume +5%), collections of Rs 19,965 Cr (+17% YoY but ~5% short of the Rs 21,000 Cr target -- the standard real-estate cash-conversion tell), and business development (new project additions) of Rs 42,100 Cr, a huge 211% of the Rs 20,000 Cr target -- this expands the launch pipeline ~35% into FY27. FY26 PAT was a record Rs 1,840-1,850 Cr (+32% YoY); EBITDA Rs 2,826 Cr (+43%, ~33.7% margin). Q4 FY26 alone: booking value Rs 10,163 Cr (highest-ever quarter, matching Q4FY25), revenue ~Rs 3,458 Cr (+63%), PAT Rs 649.5 Cr (+70%), Q4 EBITDA margin ~24.6% -- the quarter-vs-full-year margin gap (24.6% vs 33.7%) reflects normal POCM revenue-recognition lumpiness by project-completion stage, not a manipulated number. City mix for FY26 bookings is well-diversified: MMR Rs 10,313 Cr, Bengaluru Rs 8,802 Cr, NCR Rs 7,410 Cr, Pune Rs 3,659 Cr, Hyderabad Rs 2,360 Cr, others Rs 1,627 Cr -- no single-market overconcentration. Balance sheet: net debt nearly doubled to Rs 6,414 Cr (Mar-26) from Rs 3,269 Cr (Mar-25), funding the aggressive BD spend; net D/E is still a modest 0.3x (gross D/E 0.82x), cash Rs 1,861 Cr -- this is growth-funded leverage, not distress leverage, but it is a genuine step-up to watch if collections keep lagging bookings. FY27 guidance (management, business-standard.com quote from Pirojsha Godrej, 2026-05-10): BD Rs 20,000 Cr, launch value Rs 48,000 Cr, booking value >Rs 39,000 Cr (management's own quoted figure is +14% YoY on the Rs 34,171 Cr FY26 base -- note some secondary aggregator summaries round this to '20%', which conflates the booking-value growth number with the separately-guided +20% collections growth to Rs 24,000 Cr; the primary-source management quote is +14% for bookings), and a stated ROE ambition of ~20% by FY28. [INFERENCE] Current implied ROE is far below that target: Mcap Rs 64,251 Cr / P/B 3.36x implies networth of ~Rs 19,100 Cr, against FY26 PAT of ~Rs 1,850 Cr -> implied ROE of roughly 9.7%. So the FY28 ROE target requires roughly a doubling of capital efficiency within two years. [DATA] Trailing 5-year (FY21-26) presales CAGR is 38%, but FY21 was a COVID-trough base year for the whole residential sector -- this is a base-effect number, not a sustainable run-rate (V1 cycle-peak-base caveat applies squarely here). Forward, management guides +14% for FY27 bookings; Motilal Oswal's published estimate is a more conservative ~10% presales CAGR for FY26-28 'on a high base'. [DATA] Valuation as of 2026-07-13: share price ~Rs 2,162.6, market cap ~Rs 64,251 Cr, trailing P/E ~34.9x, P/B ~3.36x, 52-week range Rs 1,434-2,407.9. Analyst target consensus clusters Rs 2,100-2,800 (Morgan Stanley OW Rs 2,100; Motilal Oswal Buy Rs 2,280; Jefferies Buy Rs 2,420; HSBC Buy Rs 2,800) -- i.e. sell-side is broadly constructive despite the rich multiple. [DATA] Minor governance/regulatory noise found, none thesis-relevant at this scale: a Rs 10 lakh CGRERA penalty (Jun-2026 order, received Jul-3-2026) over pre-RERA-registration ads for project Greenvale Estate, which the company says were third-party unauthorized ads and has since secured registration; a Nagpur civil court rejecting a company/counterparty plea in an ongoing Rs 227 Cr land-title dispute (Ghogli village, Besa) that predates and is unrelated to current operating performance; and a MahaRERA refund order covering 6 buyers / 7 flats in the Godrej RKS (Chembur) project. None of these are individually or collectively material to a company booking Rs 34,000+ Cr/year. [DATA] Q1 FY27 results are NOT YET OUT as of this pass -- board meeting to approve is scheduled for 2026-08-04, with the earnings call same day at 4:30pm IST.
recommendation_rationale: This is a genuine tension case, not a clean call either way, but it resolves to Hold rather than Sell because nothing here is a broken thesis -- it's a valuation-vs-maturing-growth debate on an otherwise best-in-class operator. FOR Sell: trailing multiple (34.9x P/E, 3.36x P/B) is rich against decelerating forward growth (16% actual FY26, 14% guided FY27, ~10% analyst FY26-28 CAGR consensus -- a sharp step-down from the base-effect-inflated 38% 5yr CAGR); net debt nearly doubled YoY; collections missed target by 5% (the classic real-estate cash-conversion warning); and the current multiple effectively demands the company DOUBLE its ROE (~9.7% implied today vs ~20% FY28 target) with zero execution slippage. AGAINST Sell (i.e., why Hold and not Sell): the FY26 print itself was clean and record-setting on every operating metric (bookings, collections growth in absolute terms, PAT, EBITDA); BD execution at 211% of target is a genuine forward-growth engine (35% more launch-ready inventory into FY27), not paper promises; the balance sheet leverage remains conservative (net D/E 0.3x) and is investment-funded, not distress-funded; city-mix diversification across MMR/Bengaluru/NCR/Pune/Hyderabad reduces single-market cyclicality; promoter increased personal stake (a genuine skin-in-the-game signal); and sell-side coverage remains broadly constructive (Buy/Overweight clustered, targets above CMP). The regulatory items found (RERA ad fine, land-title litigation, MahaRERA refund) are immaterial in scale and don't change the picture. Net: rich valuation is a real risk to flag prominently, but 'expensive on a maturing growth base' is not, by itself, sufficient to force a Sell on a name executing this well operationally -- it argues for a Hold with the valuation risk explicit, not a Sell.
summary: Godrej Properties just posted its best-ever year: record pre-sales (Rs 34,171 Cr, +16%), record profit (Rs 1,850 Cr, +32%), and a huge land-bank addition (Rs 42,100 Cr of new business development, more than double its target) that sets up a bigger FY27 launch pipeline. The balance sheet took on more debt to fund that land-buying spree (net debt nearly doubled) but leverage is still conservative in relative terms, and cash collections from customers grew but missed the company's own target slightly -- a detail worth watching. Management is guiding to about 14% more pre-sales in FY27 and an ambitious near-doubling of return on equity by FY28. The stock trades at a rich ~35x trailing earnings and 3.4x book value, pricing in a good chunk of that ambition already. We rate this a Hold: nothing is broken operationally -- in fact execution has been excellent -- but the valuation leaves little room for the growth deceleration already visible in the guidance numbers (14% next year vs a much faster multi-year run before this) to disappoint further.
positive_para: FY26 was a genuinely standout year across every operating lever the market cares about in real estate: booking value (pre-sales) hit a record Rs 34,171 Cr at 105% of guidance, and business development (new land/project additions) came in at Rs 42,100 Cr -- 211% of target -- which directly expands FY27's launch-ready inventory by roughly 35%. Profitability followed: FY26 PAT of ~Rs 1,850 Cr (record, +32% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 2,826 Cr (+43%, ~33.7% margin). City-mix is diversified across MMR, Bengaluru, NCR, Pune and Hyderabad with no single-market dependence, and 11 projects each crossed Rs 1,000 Cr in bookings, evidencing depth of demand rather than one-project luck. Balance sheet leverage, while up sharply in absolute terms, remains conservative on a relative basis (net D/E ~0.3x) and is funding growth (BD/land) rather than covering shortfalls. Promoters added to their personal stake during the year, a real insider-conviction signal. Sell-side coverage remains constructive with Buy/Overweight ratings and price targets mostly above CMP (Rs 2,100-2,800 range).
negative_para: The valuation is the crux of the bear case: at ~35x trailing P/E and ~3.4x P/B, the market is capitalizing on management's own ambition of roughly doubling ROE (from an implied ~9.7% today to ~20% by FY28) and sustaining double-digit bookings growth off a much larger base -- there is very little room for execution slippage. The growth trajectory itself is decelerating: FY26 bookings grew 16%, FY27 is guided at just +14%, and independent analyst estimates (Motilal Oswal) put the FY26-28 presales CAGR at closer to 10% 'on a high base' -- a sharp step-down from the eye-catching 38% five-year CAGR, which was itself inflated by a COVID-trough FY21 base and should not be extrapolated. Collections (customer cash inflows) grew 17% but still missed the company's own Rs 21,000 Cr target by about 5% -- the classic real-estate tell of bookings running ahead of actual cash conversion. Net debt nearly doubled YoY (Rs 3,269 Cr to Rs 6,414 Cr) to fund the aggressive land-buying, a leverage trajectory that needs collections to keep pace or it compounds. Minor regulatory friction also surfaced this year (a Rs 10 lakh RERA ad-violation penalty, an ongoing Rs 227 Cr land-title dispute in Nagpur, and a MahaRERA-ordered refund on a handful of flats in one Mumbai project) -- individually immaterial, but a reminder that developer-scale execution always carries a trickle of such items.
reverse_dcf_judgment: RICH, not cheap or fair. At ~35x trailing P/E and ~3.36x P/B against an implied current ROE of only ~9.7% (PAT ~Rs 1,850 Cr / implied networth ~Rs 19,100 Cr), the multiple is not pricing today's business -- it is pricing management's own FY28 target of ~20% ROE (roughly a doubling) plus continued double-digit pre-sales growth off a base that has already grown 16% in FY26 and is guided at a slower +14% for FY27 (independent analyst consensus is closer to 10% CAGR through FY28). For the current multiple to look fair rather than rich, GPL needs near-flawless execution on BOTH the ROE ramp and sustained double-digit bookings growth simultaneously, with collections catching up to bookings (they currently lag) and net debt (which nearly doubled this year) not spiraling further. This is a name priced for a best-case outcome in a residential cycle that, by the company's own guidance cadence (16% actual -> 14% guided), looks to be past its steepest growth phase and moving into a slower, larger-base compounding phase. Not a bubble valuation given the genuine execution quality, but not cheap, and not fair-value either -- rich.
